original_question: For parameters p, q in (0, 1), characterize the two-dimensional achievement set E(p^n, q^n) consisting of all subsums of the vector series sum (p^n, q^n).
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 28 of the survey: the problem of characterizing the planar achievement sets E(p^n,q^n) for parameters p,q in (0,1). The survey’s nearby context explicitly cites the source formulation from Kula–Nowakowski [35], where it appears as Problem 2.
correct_elements: The draft already identifies the correct parameter range p,q in (0,1), the correct object E(p^n,q^n), and the correct interpretation of that object as the set of subsums of the vector geometric series sum_{n>=1} (p^n,q^n). It also correctly treats the problem as a two-dimensional achievement-set question.
missing_details: The notation should be defined explicitly: E(p^n,q^n) means E((p^n,q^n)_{n>=1}) = { sum_{n=1}^infty eps_n (p^n,q^n) : eps_n in {0,1} } subset of R^2.
The ambient space R^2 should be stated explicitly.
The paper’s intended notion of characterization is topological: determine the topological type/homeomorphism class of the achievement set, not an arbitrary descriptive characterization.
The indexing starts at n = 1; this should be made explicit.
The nearby context records the known cases: if at least one of p,q is at most 1/2, then E(p^n,q^n) is a Cantor set; if p = q >= 1/2, then E(p^n,q^n) is a line segment.
The real unresolved regime singled out by the paper is p > q > 1/2 (up to swapping coordinates), and the cited source conjectures that E(p^n,q^n) is a Cantor set there as well.
No additional algebraic hypotheses are involved here: there are no homogeneity, degree, field-characteristic, or nilpotency restrictions; the only data are the real parameters p,q in (0,1).
refined_question: For p,q in (0,1), define the planar achievement set E(p^n,q^n) := { sum_{n=1}^infty eps_n (p^n,q^n) : eps_n in {0,1} } subset of R^2. Characterize the topological type of E(p^n,q^n) for all pairs p,q in (0,1), in particular determine what happens in the remaining regime p > q > 1/2.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, after the known cases are removed, decide whether E(p^n,q^n) is a Cantor set for every p > q > 1/2.
justification: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful target. In the survey, the relevant item is Problem 28 in Section 5, and the surrounding lines show that the authors are discussing the topological nature of these planar achievement sets. The survey explicitly points to Kula–Nowakowski [35] for the concrete family E(p^n,q^n). In that source paper, Problem 2 is stated exactly as “Characterize E(p^n,q^n) for all p,q in (0,1),” and the adjoining discussion records the settled parameter ranges and isolates the open core case p > q > 1/2, conjecturing that it always gives a Cantor set. I therefore kept your question narrow, made the definition of E explicit, and added only the topological and parameter-range information needed to make it stand alone and match the paper’s actual intent.
